historical_record.description: An unreinforced brick and heavy-timber warehouse of two storeys over a basement, 275 by 258 feet, designed by Washington J. Miller and built for the hardware firm Baker & Hamilton on the site of the California Wine Association building destroyed in 1906.
Baker & Hamilton occupied the building for ten years, leaving in 1918 after merging with the Pacific Hardware & Steel Company.

unknowns.downtown-1995-2011-0021: The 1998 environmental review for 475 Brannan Street gives the building as constructed in 1908 in its summary and as begun in 1907 in its building history.
